claims.source: As a mechanism to cope with such insults and to participate in developmental tissue remodeling, hemocytes secrete ECM proteins, such as Laminins or Collagen IV (Bunt et al., 2010; Töpfer et al., 2019), as well as ECM processing enzymes or assembly factors (Martinek et al., 2008; Nelson et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bunt et al., 2010 and Töpfer et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Hemocytes secrete ECM processing enzymes and assembly factors.
claims.source: As a mechanism to cope with such insults and to participate in developmental tissue remodeling, hemocytes secrete ECM proteins, such as Laminins or Collagen IV (Bunt et al., 2010; Töpfer et al., 2019), as well as ECM processing enzymes or assembly factors (Martinek et al., 2008; Nelson et al., 1994).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Martinek et al., 2008 and Nelson et al., 1994.

claims.claim: Fat body-specific overexpression of Atf3 under the C7-GAL4 driver induced a lean phenotype and decreased lipid droplet size.
claims.source: We have reported previously that the fat body-specific overexpression of Atf3 under the C7-GAL4 driver (Koyama and Mirth, 2016) (hereafter abbreviated as C7>Atf3WT) induced a lean phenotype and decreased lipid droplet size (Rynes et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rynes et al., 2012.

claims.claim: C7>Atf3WT larvae show massive attachment of hemocytes to the adipose tissue surface.
claims.source: Intriguingly, a closer examination of C7>Atf3WT larvae in which the fat body was visualized with a help of UAS-GFP and the hemocyte population with Hml:DsRed reporter (hereafter abbreviated as Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT) revealed a massive attachment of hemocytes to the adipose tissue surface (Figure 1B, D and E), a phenotype not detected in control larvae (Figure 1A, C and E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, D, and E.

claims.claim: Fat body-associated hemocytes (FBAHs) in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae are densely packed and often form contiguous monolayers over the entire length of the adipose tissue.
claims.source: The fat body-associated hemocytes (hereafter referred to as FBAHs) present in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae were densely packed and often formed contiguous monolayers over the entire length of the adipose tissue (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The characteristic pattern of sessile hematopoietic pockets is disrupted in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae.
claims.source: In contrast, the characteristic pattern of sessile hematopoietic pockets observed in controls was disrupted in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae (Figure 1A and B), while the amount of circulating hemocytes was not significantly affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claims.claim: The amount of circulating hemocytes is not significantly affected in C7>Atf3WT larvae.
claims.source: In contrast, the characteristic pattern of sessile hematopoietic pockets observed in controls was disrupted in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae (Figure 1A and B), while the amount of circulating hemocytes was not significantly affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Hemocytes associate with clones of Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes induced by the heat shock FLPout technique.
claims.source: Importantly, we found that hemocytes also associated with clones of Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes induced by the heat shock FLPout (hsFLPout) technique (Figure 1F), suggesting that the attachment is an intrinsic property of the fat body cells with excessive Atf3 levels rather than a consequence of the systemic activation of blood cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: Hemocyte attachment to Atf3 overexpressing fat body is an intrinsic property of the fat body cells rather than a consequence of systemic activation of blood cells.
claims.source: Importantly, we found that hemocytes also associated with clones of Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes induced by the heat shock FLPout (hsFLPout) technique (Figure 1F), suggesting that the attachment is an intrinsic property of the fat body cells with excessive Atf3 levels rather than a consequence of the systemic activation of blood cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the clonal experiment data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: No uptake of GFP-positive material originating from the fat body was observed in hemocytes on C7>Atf3WT fat bodies.
claims.source: In support of this notion, neither the uptake of GFP-positive material originating from the fat body was observed in the hemocytes, nor signs of an encapsulation reaction, such as adhesion of lamellocytes or tissue melanization, were present in the case of C7>Atf3WT fat bodies (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: No signs of encapsulation reaction, such as adhesion of lamellocytes or tissue melanization, are present on C7>Atf3WT fat bodies.
claims.source: In support of this notion, neither the uptake of GFP-positive material originating from the fat body was observed in the hemocytes, nor signs of an encapsulation reaction, such as adhesion of lamellocytes or tissue melanization, were present in the case of C7>Atf3WT fat bodies (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and 1F.

claims.claim: FBAHs project filopodia of varying lengths and lamellipodia, similar to sessile hemocytes.
claims.source: Intriguingly, FBAHs, like sessile hemocytes (Lanot et al., 2001; Leitão and Sucena, 2015; Makhijani et al., 2011; Márkus et al., 2009), projected filopodia of varying lengths as well as lamellipodia (Figure 2A–B) and proliferated in situ as demonstrated by the Fly-FUCCI in vivo cell cycle reporter (Zielke et al., 2014) and immunostaining for a mitotic marker phospho-histone-H3 (pH3) (Figure 2C–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-B and citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: FBAHs proliferate in situ on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.source: Intriguingly, FBAHs, like sessile hemocytes (Lanot et al., 2001; Leitão and Sucena, 2015; Makhijani et al., 2011; Márkus et al., 2009), projected filopodia of varying lengths as well as lamellipodia (Figure 2A–B) and proliferated in situ as demonstrated by the Fly-FUCCI in vivo cell cycle reporter (Zielke et al., 2014) and immunostaining for a mitotic marker phospho-histone-H3 (pH3) (Figure 2C–D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D using the Fly-FUCCI reporter and pH3 staining.

claims.claim: The majority of FBAHs are plasmatocytes, interspersed by a smaller number of crystal cells.
claims.source: Staining against the plasmatocyte marker NimrodC1 (NimC1) (Kurucz et al., 2007a) and the crystal cell-specific BcF6:GFP reporter (Tokusumi et al., 2009) showed that like in the sessile tissue (Leitão and Sucena, 2015), the majority of the FBAHs were plasmatocytes, interspersed by a smaller number of crystal cells (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E using NimC1 and BcF6:GFP markers.

claims.claim: A portion of BcF6:GFP-positive crystal cells also stain for NimC1 and show Hml:DsRed levels similar to plasmatocytes, suggesting they are intermediate hemocytes in the process of plasmatocyte-crystal cell trans-differentiation.
claims.source: Surprisingly, a portion of the BcF6:GFP-positive crystal cells also stained for NimC1 and showed Hml:DsRed levels similar to plasmatocytes, suggesting that these cells are intermediate hemocytes in the process of plasmatocyte-crystal cell trans-differentiation (Figure 2E–E').
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 2E-E'.

claims.claim: Blackened crystal cells are observed among FBAHs in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae with the Bc1 mutation.
claims.source: Moreover, we observed blackened crystal cells among FBAHs (Figure 2F) when combining the Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT with the Bc1 mutation (Rizki et al., 1980).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claims.claim: Crystal cell differentiation likely occurs on the adipocyte surface.
claims.source: Since the runaway melanization cascade results in cell death (Lanot et al., 2001; Neyen et al., 2015), we speculate that their differentiation likely occurred on the adipocyte surface.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of melanized crystal cells and knowledge about melanization-induced cell death.

claims.claim: BcF6:GFP expressing and melanized crystal cells are mostly located within FBAH clusters and surrounded by plasmatocytes.
claims.source: Notably, both BcF6:GFP expressing and melanized crystal cells in the Bc1 background were mostly located within the FBAH clusters and were surrounded by plasmatocytes (Figure 2E–F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E-F.

claims.claim: FBAHs detach from the Atf3 overexpressing adipose tissue 48 hours after L. boulardi parasitic infection.
claims.source: We found that the FBAHs detached from the Atf3 overexpressing adipose tissue 48 hr after parasitic infection (Figure 2G–I), and lamellocyte differentiation and capsule formation (Figure 2J, L, N and P) was not impaired to a noticeable extent when compared to control larvae (Figure 2J, K, M and O).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G-I.

claims.claim: Lamellocyte differentiation and capsule formation are not impaired to a noticeable extent in Hml:DsRed, C7>Atf3WT larvae after parasitic infection compared to controls.
claims.source: We found that the FBAHs detached from the Atf3 overexpressing adipose tissue 48 hr after parasitic infection (Figure 2G–I), and lamellocyte differentiation and capsule formation (Figure 2J, L, N and P) was not impaired to a noticeable extent when compared to control larvae (Figure 2J, K, M and O).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J-P.

claims.claim: Hemocytes associated with the fat body in C7>Atf3WT larvae display a hematopoietic program reminiscent of sessile blood cells and engage in innate immune defense.
claims.source: Together, these data support the notion that hemocytes associated with the fat body in C7>Atf3WT larvae display a hematopoietic program reminiscent of sessile blood cells and engage in the innate immune defense.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations presented in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Drosophila larval adipocytes are the primary source of basement membrane components for most internal organs, including their own.
claims.source: The Drosophila larval adipocytes are the primary source of the basement membrane components for most internal organs (Pastor-Pareja and Xu, 2011), including their own.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pastor-Pareja and Xu, 2011.

claims.claim: Hindering ECM protein secretion and release can lead to fibrotic accumulation.
claims.source: Hindering ECM protein secretion and release can lead to fibrotic accumulation (Shahab et al., 2015; Zang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shahab et al., 2015 and Zang et al., 2015.

claims.claim: Atf3 has a role in cellular trafficking in epithelial cells.
claims.source: Given the described role of Atf3 in cellular trafficking in epithelial cells (Donohoe et al., 2018), we asked whether the attachment of hemocytes to the Atf3 overexpressing fat body could be caused by changes in the structure or composition of the basement membrane.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Donohoe et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Atf3 overexpression in clonal adipocytes leads to accumulation of Collagen IV, Laminin, and Multiplexin below the basement membrane.
claims.source: Indeed, the visualization of the Vkg::GFP reporter, a fusion protein of Collagen IVα2 and GFP (Morin et al., 2001), as well as immunostaining against Laminin and the Collagen XV/XVIII-type protein Multiplexin (Mp) revealed accumulation of ECM below the basement membrane in Atf3 overexpressing clonal adipocytes (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: C7>Atf3WT fat bodies form deep pericellular folds containing electron-dense material.
claims.source: Transmission-electron microscopy (TEM) further showed that in contrast to the mostly smooth cell membranes of control adipocytes (Figure 3E), the C7>Atf3WT fat bodies formed deep pericellular folds containing electron-dense material (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by TEM data shown in Figure 3E-F.

claims.claim: ECM proteins are trapped in pericellular spaces in Atf3 overexpressing fat bodies, which might attract hemocytes to the fat body surface.
claims.source: These data suggest that the ECM proteins are trapped in pericellular spaces, which might attract hemocytes to the fat body surface.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of ECM accumulation in pericellular spaces.

claims.claim: Mp knockdown in Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes results in restoration of the stereotypical pattern of sessile hematopoietic pockets at the body wall.
claims.source: Importantly, Mp knockdown in Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes resulted in restoration of the stereotypical pattern of the sessile hematopoietic pockets at the body wall (Figure 3L–O), supporting a notion that upon fat body-specific Atf3 overexpression hemocytes residing in the sessile pockets relocate and expand on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3L-O.

claims.claim: Upon fat body-specific Atf3 overexpression, hemocytes residing in the sessile pockets relocate and expand on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.source: Importantly, Mp knockdown in Atf3 overexpressing adipocytes resulted in restoration of the stereotypical pattern of the sessile hematopoietic pockets at the body wall (Figure 3L–O), supporting a notion that upon fat body-specific Atf3 overexpression hemocytes residing in the sessile pockets relocate and expand on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Mp knockdown restores sessile pockets while abolishing FBAHs.

claims.claim: There is a functional link between ECM accumulation and hemocyte attachment to the fat body.
claims.source: These results demonstrate a functional link between ECM accumulation and hemocyte attachment to the fat body, and uncover Mp as a key component of this interaction.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that ECM manipulation affects hemocyte attachment.

claims.claim: Mp is a key component of the interaction between ECM accumulation and hemocyte attachment.
claims.source: These results demonstrate a functional link between ECM accumulation and hemocyte attachment to the fat body, and uncover Mp as a key component of this interaction.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Mp's necessity for hemocyte attachment.

claims.claim: Loss of Eater completely abolishes sessile hematopoietic pockets, increasing the number of circulating hemocytes.
claims.source: While little is known about the interaction that anchors the hemocytes to the epidermis, a loss of the plasmatocyte-specific phagocytosis receptor Eater (Kocks et al., 2005) was shown to completely abolish sessile pockets, increasing the number of circulating hemocytes (Bretscher et al., 2015; Melcarne et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bretscher et al., 2015 and Melcarne et al., 2019.

claims.claim: C7>Atf3WT larvae homozygous for the eater1 loss of function allele lack both sessile hematopoietic pockets and FBAHs.
claims.source: To address the requirement of Eater in FBAH attachment, we generated C7>Atf3WT larvae homozygous for the eater1 loss of function allele. Strikingly, these larvae lacked both sessile hematopoietic pockets and FBAHs (Figure 4A–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-E.

claims.claim: Silencing Eater expression in C7>Atf3WT fat bodies does not interfere with hemocyte-fat body interaction.
claims.source: To validate a specific requirement for Eater in the hemocytes, we first silenced its expression in C7>Atf3WT fat bodies, which did not interfere with hemocyte-fat body interaction (Figure 4F–G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F-G.

claims.claim: Simultaneous Atf3 overexpression and Eater knockdown in hemocytes impairs FBAH formation.
claims.source: Next, we generated larvae which aside from C7-GAL4 also carried the HmlΔ-GAL4 hemocyte-specific driver (Sinenko and Mathey-Prevot, 2004). While the expression of Atf3 in both the fat body and the hemocytes did not markedly impact hemocyte adhesion (Figure 4H), simultaneous Atf3 overexpression and Eater knockdown impaired FBAH formation (Figure 4I–J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I-J.

claims.claim: Eater is a hemocyte-specific adhesion molecule that acts both in the context of sessile pockets and hemocytes on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.source: These data define Eater as a hemocyte-specific adhesion molecule that acts both in the context of the sessile pockets and the hemocytes on the adipose tissue surface.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Eater's requirement in both contexts.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Mp in epidermal cells drastically disrupts the pattern of sessile tissue.
claims.source: To this end, we silenced Mp with the a58-GAL4 (larval epidermis), mef2-GAL4 (body wall muscles) and elav-GAL4 (neurons) (Galko and Krasnow, 2004; Lin and Goodman, 1994; Ranganayakulu et al., 1996) drivers to account for the fact that the pockets reside between the larval epidermis and the body wall muscle layer, and their maintenance depends on the activity of peripheral neurons (Makhijani et al., 2011). While loss of Mp in the epidermal cells drastically disrupted the pattern of sessile tissue, resulting in a phenotype strikingly resembling that of eater1 (Figure 4K–O), Mp knockdown in the muscles and the neurons did not result in a similar dispersion of the sessile tissue (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4K-O.

claims.claim: Mp knockdown in muscles and neurons does not result in dispersion of sessile tissue.
claims.source: To this end, we silenced Mp with the a58-GAL4 (larval epidermis), mef2-GAL4 (body wall muscles) and elav-GAL4 (neurons) (Galko and Krasnow, 2004; Lin and Goodman, 1994; Ranganayakulu et al., 1996) drivers to account for the fact that the pockets reside between the larval epidermis and the body wall muscle layer, and their maintenance depends on the activity of peripheral neurons (Makhijani et al., 2011). While loss of Mp in the epidermal cells drastically disrupted the pattern of sessile tissue, resulting in a phenotype strikingly resembling that of eater1 (Figure 4K–O), Mp knockdown in the muscles and the neurons did not result in a similar dispersion of the sessile tissue (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-D.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Col4a1 and Trol in the epidermis does not mimic the loss of sessile tissue structure caused by Mp knockdown.
claims.source: Interestingly, although effective in suppressing FBAHs on Atf3 overexpressing adipose tissues, knockdown of Col4a1 and Trol in the epidermis did not mimic the loss of sessile tissue structure inflicted by Mp knockdown (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E–1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E-F.

claims.claim: Silencing Mp specifically in hemocytes has no visible impact on the integrity of sessile hematopoietic pockets.
claims.source: Furthermore, silencing Mp specifically in hemocytes had no visible impact on the integrity of the sessile hematopoietic pockets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G–1H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G-H.

claims.claim: Eater and Mp are required to facilitate hemocyte-basement membrane interactions both in sessile hematopoietic pockets and the de novo hematopoietic compartment on Atf3 overexpressing fat bodies.
claims.source: These results highlight a requirement for Eater and Mp to facilitate hemocyte-basement membrane interactions both in the case of the naturally occurring sessile hematopoietic pockets and the de novo hematopoietic compartment on Atf3 overexpressing fat bodies.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing the necessity of both proteins in both contexts.

claims.claim: Drosophila Mp consists of an N-terminal Thrombospondin-like domain, a Collagen triple helix domain, an NC1 trimerization domain, and a C-terminal Endostatin-domain.
claims.source: The Drosophila Mp consists of an N-terminal Thrombospondin-like domain, followed by a Collagen triple helix domain, an NC1 trimerization domain and the C-terminal Endostatin-domain, all of which are present in its mammalian counterparts, Collagens XV and XVIII (Heljasvaara et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Heljasvaara et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Mp expression initiates during late embryonic development, mostly in the heart tube and central nervous system, and is needed for motoaxonal pathfinding.
claims.source: Mp expression initiates during late embryonic development, mostly in the heart tube and the central nervous system, and is needed for motoaxonal pathfinding (Harpaz et al., 2013; Meyer and Moussian, 2009).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Harpaz et al., 2013 and Meyer and Moussian, 2009.

claims.claim: Mp levels markedly increase in the basement membrane of C7>Mp::GFP fat body.
claims.source: Compared to control, Mp levels markedly increased in the basement membrane of C7>Mp::GFP fat body (Figure 5A–B) as determined by immunostaining with a Mp-specific antibody (Harpaz et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: GFP signal from Mp::GFP is restricted to the adipocyte cytoplasm, suggesting that the C-terminal end of Mp undergoes proteolytic cleavage.
claims.source: However, GFP signal was restricted to the adipocyte cytoplasm (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that the C-terminal end of Mp undergoes proteolytic cleavage.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that GFP signal is cytoplasmic while Mp staining is in the basement membrane.

claims.claim: Mp::GFP overexpression in the fat body does not induce hemocyte adhesion.
claims.source: Surprisingly, Mp::GFP overexpression in the fat body did not induce hemocyte adhesion (Figure 5A–B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: Mp::GFP overexpression in the fat body leads to complete dispersal of sessile hematopoietic pockets, phenocopying homozygous eater1 mutants.
claims.source: Instead, it led to the complete dispersal of the sessile hematopoietic pockets, phenocopying homozygous eater1 mutants (Figure 5C–E, compare to Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claims.claim: Circulating hemocyte numbers in C7>Mp::GFP larvae significantly increase compared to controls, reaching similar levels as in eater1 mutants.
claims.source: In addition, circulating hemocyte numbers in C7>Mp::GFP larvae significantly increased compared to controls, reaching similar levels as in eater1 mutants (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Mp protein levels increase notably in the circulation of C7>Mp::GFP larvae relative to controls.
claims.source: Immunoblots from the cell free hemolymph revealed a notable increase of the Mp protein in the circulation of C7>Mp::GFP larvae relative to controls (Figure 5G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claims.claim: Fat-body-produced Mp incorporates into the adipocyte ECM and is also released into the hemolymph where it may interfere with hemocyte binding to basement membrane due to a saturation effect.
claims.source: These results indicate that while fat-body-produced Mp incorporates into the adipocyte ECM, it is also released into the hemolymph where it may interact with hemocytes and interfere with their binding to the basement membrane due to a saturation effect.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that Mp overexpression prevents hemocyte attachment despite Mp incorporation into the ECM.

claims.claim: Clonal adipocytes overexpressing Mp::GFP are surrounded by hemocytes that display characteristics of FBAHs.
claims.source: To circumvent the hemolymph overload, we induced Mp::GFP expression only in clones, which resulted in local Mp accumulation over the targeted adipocytes and in their intercellular spaces (Figure 6A–E). Strikingly, clonal adipocytes overexpressing Mp::GFP were surrounded by hemocytes, which displayed previously established characteristics of FBAHs, namely tight clustering and projection of filopodia and lamellipodia, the ability to undergo mitosis on the tissue surface and the presence of crystal cells (Figure 6C–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-E.

claims.claim: Mp::GFP expression in the pouch region of the wing disc promotes hemocyte adhesion to this specific domain.
claims.source: Moreover, Mp::GFP expression in the pouch region of the wing disc using the nubbin-Gal4, UAS-mCherry driver (nub>mCherry) promoted hemocyte adhesion to this specific domain (Figure 6F–G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F-G.

claims.claim: Hemocyte-epithelial tissue association induced by Mp::GFP expression in wing disc is not provoked by apoptosis of imaginal cells.
claims.source: Of note, this hemocyte epithelial tissue association was not provoked by apoptosis of imaginal cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claims.claim: Mp is not only necessary but also sufficient to facilitate hemocyte attachment to tissue surfaces.
claims.source: Together these results demonstrate that Mp is not only necessary but also sufficient to facilitate hemocyte attachment to tissue surfaces.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing both loss-of-function and gain-of-function effects of Mp.

claims.claim: Mp::FLAG co-precipitates with Eater::GFP from Drosophila S2 cell lysates.
claims.source: To this end, we performed co-immunoprecipitation experiments with tagged Eater::GFP and Mp::FLAG proteins in S2 cells, and found that the two proteins indeed co-precipitated (Figure 6H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H.

claims.claim: Mp acts as an interacting partner of Eater on the basement membranes of C7>Atf3WT fat bodies and on the epidermal surface covering sessile hematopoietic pockets.
claims.source: While we cannot exclude that the binding might be indirect, these results present an argument that Mp acts as an interacting partner of Eater on the basement membranes of C7>Atf3WT fat bodies, and on the epidermal surface covering the sessile hematopoietic pockets (Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-immunoprecipitation data and functional studies.

claims.claim: Fundamental principles of hematopoiesis and hematopoietic niche formation show similarities across phyla.
claims.source: Fundamental principles of hematopoiesis and hematopoietic niche formation show similarities across phyla (Martinez-Agosto et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Martinez-Agosto et al., 2007.

claims.claim: Atf3 overexpression in adipocytes promotes the formation of a de novo hematopoietic compartment on the adipose tissue surface at the expense of the naturally occurring sessile hematopoietic cell pool.
claims.source: We show that Atf3 overexpression in adipocytes promotes the formation of a de novo hematopoietic compartment on the adipose tissue surface at the expense of the naturally occurring sessile hematopoietic cell pool (Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main finding supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: FBAHs show round/spherical morphology and project short filopodia and lamellipodia, which are characteristic of sessile hemocytes.
claims.source: The fat body-associated hemocytes showed round/spherical morphology, and projected short filopodia and lamellipodia, which are characteristic to the sessile hemocytes (Lanot et al., 2001, Figure 2B) and hemocytes adhering to Laminin-coated substrates (Sampson and Williams, 2012), but are distinct from the elongated phenotype of the migratory embryonic macrophages and the pupal hemocytes assisting tissue remodeling (Evans and Wood, 2011; Sampson et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The characteristic morphology and absence of tissue debris-phagocytosis and encapsulation response suggest that FBAHs are in a naïve homeostatic state, not engaged in immune response.
claims.source: The characteristic morphology and the absence of tissue debris-phagocytosis and encapsulation response suggest that FBAHs are in a naïve homeostatic state, not engaged in immune response.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the morphological and functional observations of FBAHs.

claims.claim: Hemocytes proliferate in the circulation, but the division rate of those in sessile pockets is higher due to stimulating effects of Activin-β secreted by peripheral sensory neurons.
claims.source: Although hemocytes also proliferate in the circulation, the division rate of those in the sessile pockets was shown to be higher due to the stimulating effects of Activin-β secreted by peripheral sensory neurons (Makhijani et al., 2017; Makhijani et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Makhijani et al., 2017 and Makhijani et al., 2011.

claims.claim: The proliferation of FBAHs may be part of a hemocyte-autonomous developmental program supported by physical adhesion to tissue and cell-cell contacts between attached hemocytes.
claims.source: Since the fat body lacks the innervation of the epidermal cells, the proliferation of FBAHs may be part of a hemocyte-autonomous developmental program, which is supported by the physical adhesion to the tissue and cell-cell contacts between attached hemocytes.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation that FBAHs proliferate despite lack of neuronal innervation.

claims.claim: Cell-cell contacts are instrumental in the trans-differentiation of plasmatocytes to crystal cells in sessile pockets, which requires Serrate-Notch juxtacrine signaling.
claims.source: Such contacts appear instrumental in the trans-differentiation of plasmatocytes to crystal cells in the sessile pockets, which requires Serrate-Notch juxtacrine signaling among the clustered cells (Leitão and Sucena, 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Leitão and Sucena, 2015.

claims.claim: Plasmatocyte-crystal cell trans-differentiation in FBAH clusters is cluster-dependent and does not require signals secreted by peripheral neurons.
claims.source: Similarly, FBAH clusters contained fully and partially differentiated crystal cells intermingled with the hemocytes, which suggests that plasmatocyte-crystal cell trans-differentiation is cluster-dependent and does not require signals secreted by peripheral neurons.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of crystal cells in FBAH clusters despite lack of neuronal innervation.

claims.claim: The simultaneous appearance of FBAHs and decline of sessile hemocytes does not significantly impact the amount of circulating blood cells.
claims.source: Importantly, the simultaneous appearance of the FBAHs and a decline of the sessile hemocytes did not significantly impact the amount of circulating blood cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: FBAHs are dynamic, entering and leaving the circulation at a comparable rate to sessile hemocytes.
claims.source: This may indicate that FBAHs are dynamic, entering and leaving the circulation at a comparable rate to sessile hemocytes (Honti et al., 2010; Makhijani et al., 2011; Welman et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that circulating hemocyte numbers remain stable despite FBAH formation, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Col4a1 and Trol strongly suppresses fat body association of hemocytes in Atf3 overexpressing fat bodies.

results.result: Atf3 overexpression in adipocytes induces hemocyte relocation from sessile pockets to the fat body surface, creating a de novo hematopoietic compartment. This relocation is an intrinsic property of Atf3-expressing adipocytes and is functionally linked to ECM accumulation, specifically involving Multiplexin (Mp).
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C40 provide direct experimental evidence of hemocyte attachment to Atf3-overexpressing fat bodies with appropriate controls and quantification (C35, Figure 1B-E). Claims C60-C63 demonstrate that Mp knockdown abolishes this phenotype and restores sessile pockets, establishing functional necessity. The clonal experiments (C39-C40) effectively rule out systemic effects. The conclusion (C90) is well-supported by converging lines of evidence.

results.result: Fat body-associated hemocytes (FBAHs) display functional characteristics similar to sessile hemocytes, including proliferation, differentiation into crystal cells, and ability to respond to immune challenges.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C44 demonstrate FBAH morphology and proliferation with appropriate markers (Fly-FUCCI, pH3). Claims C45-C49 show hemocyte composition and differentiation using validated markers (NimC1, BcF6:GFP). Claims C50-C51 demonstrate immune responsiveness through parasitic wasp infection experiments. The characterization is comprehensive with multiple independent assays supporting the conclusion (C52).

results.result: Atf3 overexpression causes ECM accumulation in pericellular spaces of adipocytes, with Multiplexin being specifically required for hemocyte attachment while other ECM components (Col4a1, Trol, Vkg) play supporting structural roles.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C57 provide direct visualization of ECM accumulation using multiple markers (Vkg::GFP, Laminin, Mp) and TEM. Claims C99-C106 systematically test different ECM components through RNAi knockdown, showing Mp's unique requirement (C103) while other components affect tissue integrity but not specifically hemocyte attachment. The inference that membrane fold content rather than structure drives attachment (C105) is well-supported by the observation that folds persist after Mp knockdown without hemocyte binding.

results.result: Eater on hemocytes and Multiplexin in basement membranes physically interact and are both necessary and sufficient for hemocyte-tissue association in both sessile pockets and FBAHs.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C68 demonstrate Eater's hemocyte-specific requirement through tissue-specific knockdown and rescue experiments. Claims C69-C72 show Mp's epidermis-specific requirement for sessile pocket formation. Claim C87 provides biochemical evidence of physical interaction through co-immunoprecipitation. The necessity is well-established through loss-of-function (C65, C69), and sufficiency is demonstrated by gain-of-function experiments in subsequent results. The conclusion (C73, C88) integrates multiple lines of evidence.

results.result: Multiplexin is sufficient to induce hemocyte attachment when expressed clonally, but whole-tissue overexpression disrupts sessile pockets through a saturation effect involving Mp release into hemolymph.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C82 document the paradoxical effect of whole-tissue Mp overexpression, with appropriate controls and hemolymph analysis (C81). Claims C83-C85 demonstrate sufficiency through clonal expression and wing disc experiments. The saturation mechanism (C82, C109) is a reasonable inference from the contrasting phenotypes, though direct binding competition is not demonstrated. The conclusion of sufficiency (C86) is well-supported by the clonal data, while the proposed mechanism remains speculative but plausible.

results.result: Background context on hematopoiesis in mammals and Drosophila, establishing the biological framework and prior knowledge for the study.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1-C33, C89, C107) provide literature context through appropriate citations to establish the biological background. They accurately represent prior work on mammalian HSC niches (C8-C14), Drosophila hematopoiesis (C15-C28), and hemocyte behavior (C29-C33). These are standard background claims appropriately supported by citations rather than new experimental findings.

results.result: Molecular characterization and evolutionary context of Multiplexin and Eater, including their structural domains, expression patterns, and mammalian orthologs.
results.evaluation: Claims about Mp structure (C74), expression (C75), and mammalian orthologs (C112-C117) are supported by appropriate citations. Claims about Eater's family membership (C118-C120) are similarly well-cited. The speculation about Mp-Eater interaction mechanisms (C121) is appropriately qualified as speculation. These provide important molecular context but are primarily literature-based rather than novel findings.
